working_title: Joint identifiability of underdetermined post-nonlinear mixtures across regimes: Support coverage and intersection lattices
known_information: source count n and sparsity level k
componentwise real-analytic strict monotonicity and zero-preservation of each f_r
an input-scale-normalized function class for every regime
observation-domain calibration uniqueness for the population lifting theorem
parametric PNL family and frozen estimator thresholds in finite-sample experiments
unknown_information: source signals, sparse supports and isolated-zone labels
scale_normalization: If f and f(D^{-1}z) both belong to the selected class, then D=I. The experimental family f(z)=z+beta*tanh(z), beta>-1, satisfies this condition by its unit asymptotic slope. This removes diagonal scale only, not general nonlinear reparameterization.
calibration_uniqueness: Every observationally equivalent representation in the model class must have the same linearized variable up to a diagonal sensor scale and global source permutation-column scaling. Real analyticity and nonempty open observation intervals extend the scale relation so normalization forces D_r=I. This is an independent population assumption, not a conclusion from rich isolated zones.
calibration_counterexample: For A=[I_4, ones], H(z)=z+z^3 preserves the separating support subspaces. The alternative g=f(H^{-1}z) remains in the general normalized analytic class but gives nonlinearly reparameterized sources. Therefore normalization and support geometry alone do not prove calibration uniqueness.
unnormalized_ambiguity: For any positive diagonal D, (A,f_r) and (DA,f_r(D^{-1}z)) induce identical noiseless observations with unchanged sources and supports but generically different column directions.
cross_regime_coupling: A is shared across regimes, and calibration uniqueness plus normalized analytic continuation forces every residual regime-specific row scale D_r to be I before support subspaces are pooled
source_assumption: k-sparse sources with connected relatively open support domains and regime-specific, potentially incomplete support coverage
global_coverage_requirement: For each source i, the intersection of all supports containing i is {i}; the unlabelled depth-k intersection lattice recovers exactly the identifiable column directions
source_recovery_requirement: After A is identified, the sparse representation is unique under 2k < spark(A)
stability_result: A local deterministic bound for one approximate intersection; no recursive depth-k propagation or end-to-end statistical rate is claimed
negative_control_model: x_t = f_{r_t}(A_{r_t}s_t) with arbitrary unrelated A_r and no cross-regime constraint; increasing R alone does not remove per-regime ambiguity
equivalence_class: A global permutation and nonsingular diagonal scaling of source columns, with corresponding inverse scalings of sources; f_r is identified on its observation domain only under calibration uniqueness

experiment_evidence_scope.five_source: End-to-end blind PNL calibration, depth-2 direction recovery and noise-aware sparse recovery; oracle inversion is only a control; PNL-SCA-SSZ and online dictionary learning are explicitly adapted baselines
experiment_evidence_scope.random_support: Random separating support families with the same normalized calibrator and both baselines; not evidence restricted to the original {1,5}/{2,5} configuration
experiment_evidence_scope.higher_order: Linear support-subspace geometry showing depth-3 recovery versus pairwise failure; no PNL calibration claim
experiment_evidence_scope.scaling: Noiseless linear direction estimation and OMP source recovery; not a scalable high-dimensional PNL claim
experiment_evidence_scope.lattice_complexity: Noiseless population subspaces varying k and multi-source prototype count; no PNL calibration, source recovery or pruning claim
experiment_evidence_scope.conditioning: Different accepted matrix ensembles with angle quartiles and post-hoc operational failure attribution; not a same-matrix dose response
experiment_evidence_scope.measured_speech: Measured source waveforms with synthetic activation blocks, shared mixing and regime-specific PNL distortions; not real-mixture validation

out_of_scope: a merely C1 generalization or calibration uniqueness derived from rich isolated zones alone
unknown source count or sparsity level
unnormalized physical mixing-direction claims without external sensor calibration
higher-sparsity or non-full-spark guarantees beyond 2k < spark(A)
recursive depth-k stability or statistical consistency rates combining calibration and intersection errors
claims of real-world recovery without independently recorded PNL mixtures and source-level ground truth
